results.summary_before: This project implements a custom 8-bit microprocessor inspired by the 6502, built around an ALU, registers and a microcoded instruction decoder that executes a subset of the original instruction set. Data is exchanged on the eight bidirectional pins uio[0] to uio[7], while the eight outputs uo[0] to uo[7] carry address bits, and the design runs at 40 MHz. The documentation mentions a block diagram and describes two testing strategies for verifying processor correctness. No silicon test results are reported, and the instruction subset is not fully enumerated in the provided text.

results.summary_before: This mixed-signal design is a 31-stage ring oscillator with controllable current sources, providing divided clock outputs. It is enabled via a ring_enb signal, and when ui_in is set to 0xFF, the oscillator runs and produces divided frequencies on the outputs. The design includes analog control pins for current sources and power, and it can be tested with an oscilloscope to measure timing. The documentation is brief, indicating it was created for the TTIHP26a shuttle, but lacks detailed test results or application notes.

results.summary_before: This design animates a snake travelling around a 7-segment display. A chain of flip-flops driven by the clock and reset generates a time sequence, and each step lights the segments that form the moving snake. A step button advances the snake by one tile, and the design uses the 7-segment segments A through G plus the decimal point as outputs. The documentation is brief and the external hardware section is left as an unfilled template, but the behaviour is clear from the description.
